title: Tikal Temple II
note: Temple of the Masks, built c. AD 700 for Lady Kalajuun Une' Mo'; three levels; faces Temple I (es.wikipedia, Wikipedia).

title: Tikal Temple I
note: Temple of the Great Jaguar, funerary temple of Jasaw Chan K'awiil I; nine levels; faces west across the Great Plaza (Wikipedia).

title: Tikal Temple V
note: c. AD 700; seven 4 m levels; its stair rises from the north, unusually for Tikal (Wikipedia).

title: Mundo Perdido Pyramid (Tikal)
note: The Lost World pyramid, 31 m on a 67.5 m base; stairs east and west to the top, north and south to the 8th of 10 levels; final Teotihuacan-influenced form c. AD 250 (Wikipedia).

title: Tikal Temple IV
note: Temple of the Double-Headed Serpent, c. 741; the tallest Maya structure of its age; seven levels; faces east (Wikipedia).

title: Tikal Temple III
note: Temple of the Jaguar Priest, dated 810 by Stela 24; nine levels; faces east to the Great Plaza (Wikipedia).

title: El Castillo (Temple of Kukulcán)
note: Nine terraces (24 m) and a 6 m temple on a 55.3 m square base, a stairway on each side; built between the 8th and 12th centuries (Wikipedia).

title: Temple of the Inscriptions (Palenque)
note: 22.8 m stepped pyramid, eight levels plus the temple; Pakal's funerary monument, finished shortly after 683 (es/en.wikipedia).

title: Pyramid of the Moon (Teotihuacán)
note: 43 m on a 147 × 130 m base, built in stages from before AD 200 to 450; faces south down the Avenue of the Dead; five levels as restored (approximate).

title: Pyramid of the Sun (Teotihuacán)
note: 65 m today (75 m complete) on a ~225 m base, built about AD 200; faces west onto the Avenue of the Dead; five levels as restored (approximate).
